subject: humanities
passage: Rongorongo, a script of carved glyphs that survives on about two dozen wooden tablets and staffs from Rapa Nui (Easter Island), most of them collected by European visitors in the late 1800s, has resisted every attempt at decipherment. By the time outsiders became interested in the glyphs, few if any islanders could still read them. Scholars therefore continue to debate whether ______ records full sentences of the Rapa Nui language or serves mainly as a memory aid for people reciting chants.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The thing that either "records full sentences" or "serves as a memory aid" is the script, "Rongorongo," a singular noun named at the start. The blank is the subject of the clause, so it needs a singular subject pronoun: "it." The plural nouns "tablets," "staffs" and "glyphs" are tempting, but they are not what the scholars are debating, and the singular verbs "records" and "serves" confirm a singular subject.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "They" is plural, but the antecedent is the singular "Rongorongo"; "they records" also breaks agreement.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Them" is plural and is an object pronoun, so it can't serve as the subject of "records."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Itself" is a reflexive pronoun, which can't act as the subject of a clause.
explanation.D: Correct. The singular subject pronoun "it" refers back to "Rongorongo" and agrees with "records" and "serves."
